[[Category:Random variable| ]]
A '''random variable''' is a [[variable]] whose value is probabilistic.

== Formal definition ==

[[Function]]

$$
X:(\Omega,\mathcal{F}(\Omega)) \to (S,\mathcal{F}(S)),
$$

is a '''random variable''' if

* $\Omega=\{\omega\}$ is a '''[[sample space]]'''
* $S=X(\Omega)$ is the [[set]] of all possible values of $X$, known as the '''value space'''.
* $\mathcal{F}(\Omega),\mathcal{F}(S)$ are [[sigma-algebra]]s of $\Omega,S$ respectively

{{Hidden example}}
Let $\Omega=\mathbb{R}$, then

$$
X(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
1,&\omega\text{ is even},\\
0,&\omega\text{ is odd}.
\end{cases}
$$

is a '''random variable''' with value space $S=\{0,1\}$.
{{End hidden}}

== Probability distribution ==

Let $P_\Omega$ be the [[probability space#Probability_measure|probability measure]] of $(\Omega,\mathcal{F}(\Omega))$,

then the '''probability measure''' of $(S,\mathcal{F}(S))$

$$
P_X: \mathcal{F}(S) \to [0,1], \\
P_X(S)=1, \\
\forall \omega_i \in \Omega: P_X(X(\omega_i))=P_\Omega(\omega_i)).
$$

$P_X$ is then known as the '''probability distribution''' of random variable $X$.

=== Property ===

For $B \subseteq S$

$$
P_X(X\in B)=P_\Omega(\{\omega\in\Omega:X(\omega)\in B\}).
$$
